intro_md: 1 October 2026. Your revision of Chapters 1–7, from the Word file *The Ruler of Nothing – Chapters 1-7*, put in house style (straight quotes, `---` for section breaks). The chapter as it stood before is saved as `Drafts/Chapter 1 - A War Without Sound (Draft 3, before the author's revision of 1 October).md`. Every change here is yours. changes.title: His fingers come back wet and gritty
changes.before: Something warm slid from his hair down the side of his temple. He touched it with a shaking hand. His fingers came back smeared with mud and something darker. A stiff lock of hair had fallen across his eyes; he pushed it aside with the heel of his palm.
changes.after: Something warm slid from his hair down the side of his temple. He touched it with a shaking hand. His fingers came back wet and gritty. A stiff lock of hair had fallen across his eyes; he pushed it aside with the heel of his palm.
changes.why: Plainer. "Something darker" leaned on the reader to think *blood*, and the warm trickle already says it.
changes.decision_note: Your edit, from the Word file of 1 October.

changes.title: Gerolt's first question
changes.before: "Didn't catch that. Try using more than one syllable. You've got a whole mouth back there."
changes.why: Drops the one-syllable joke at a boy who can barely speak. Gerolt's humour is still there two lines up ("I'm too old to catch you twice in one day") and two lines down (his back).
changes.decision_note: Your edit, from the Word file of 1 October.

changes.title: Gerolt's name, without the joke
changes.before: "My farm. In Mydea." His eyes moved towards the shuttered window before returning to the boy. "Gerolt, by the way. Seeing as it's my roof you've woken up under, seemed only polite to introduce myself before you started asking it questions."
changes.after: "My farm. In Mydea." His eyes moved towards the shuttered window before returning to the boy. "Gerolt, by the way."
changes.why: Shorter, and his name lands on its own.
changes.decision_note: Your edit, from the Word file of 1 October.

changes.title: "Then why can't I feel it?"
changes.before: "You said it already belongs to me." The words came faster now, and once they started he found he couldn't slow them back down. "You said I'd feel it. I don't feel fire. I don't feel water. I don't feel earth or wind or some fifth thing you haven't mentioned because you're hoping I won't need it. I feel a fire that isn't mine, and wind that isn't mine, and a headache that's at least probably my own, and that is the whole list, Gerolt. That is every single thing I have."
changes.after: "You said it already belongs to me." The words came faster now, and once they started he found he couldn't slow them back down. "Then why can't I feel it? I can feel your fire, and the wind coming through your shutters, and a headache that's at least probably my own. I'm trying, Gerolt. There's nothing else."
changes.why: He pleads now instead of listing. It's simpler, but it takes out "a headache that's at least probably my own", the line the principles use to show his humour survives, and it was his only joke in the chapter. See the review, question 1. *Round 2 (1 October):* the author agreed Claude's recommendation (review question 1).
changes.decision_note: Your edit, from the Word file of 1 October, then Claude's recommendation on review question 1, which you agreed.
changes.decision_short: your Word file, then review question 1.

changes.title: Gerolt answers "What about someone with none?"
changes.before: "I keep hoping if I say the right thing, something in you will just—answer," he said at last. "Like calling a dog that's wandered off. Maybe it didn't hear you the first time."
changes.after: "I don't know what they'd do with you," he said at last. "I keep hoping if I say the right thing, something in you will just—answer. Like calling a dog that's wandered off. Maybe it didn't hear you the first time."
changes.why: Better: the boy's question used to go unanswered. Now Gerolt answers it honestly before he turns to hoping.
changes.decision_note: Your edit, from the Word file of 1 October.

changes.title: "By the thousands"
changes.before: "Aye. By the thousands." Gerolt did not turn around. "That's what won't sit right in me."
changes.after: "Aye. By the thousands." Gerolt did not turn around.
changes.why: "That's what won't sit right in me" is gone, and the next line carries it.

changes.title: Gerolt can't make it fit
changes.before: "So either I've been wrong about how the world works for sixty years, or something out there made it true just long enough to kill every one of them."
changes.after: "I know what I saw, lad, and I still can't make it fit."
changes.why: "I've never seen that" repeats what he said three lines up ("I never saw men fight beside beastfolk"), and "shoulder to shoulder" repeats what the boy has just seen. See the review, question 2. *Round 2 (1 October):* the author agreed Claude's recommendation (review question 2).

changes.title: "That person came to stop me"
changes.before: "How could I know?" His voice came out level and far too quiet. "I woke surrounded by bodies. Every one of them was there to fight. Why would that one be any different?" The answer was out before he could hold it back. "I was what they came to stop."
changes.after: "How could I know?" His voice came out level and far too quiet. "I woke surrounded by bodies. Every one of them was there to fight. Why would that one be any different?" The answer was out before he could hold it back. "That person came to stop me, Gerolt."
changes.why: Plainer and more personal than "I was what they came to stop", and he says it to Gerolt. It's still only his belief, which is right for him.
